newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-ALLENBY PLANS TO PLEASE PARENTS IN PARIS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ALLENBY PLANS TO PLEASE PARENTS IN PARIS.

text.p: Australian Robert Allenby has flown his parents to Paris for the French Open which starts on Thursday so they can see where he had one of his greatest triumphs in a relatively short European Tour career.
His sudden-death playoff victory over Bernhard Langer last year was one of Allenby's outstanding memories from four Tour wins, three of them in 1996.
Allenby's form was so convincing that he could have challenged Colin Montgomerie for the European number one title but for two serious accidents at the end of the year.
First, he damaged an ankle severely and then broke his sternum in a car accident while recuperating from the first injury.
He had to resort to hitting the now well-documented painful tapped shot just a few yards off the first at Valderrama before immediately retiring from the end-of-season Volvo Masters.
That shot ensured he took third place in the rankings behind Montgomerie and Ian Woosnam.

By his own admittance he tried to come back from the second injury too quickly and despite fashioning seventh and eighth places in the first two events on the European Tour, both in Australia, Allenby has been waiting to get back on a roll.
Disciplined gym work has helped him back and he took ninth place in Hamburg recently where he had won in the past. But he had his second missed cut in majors this year with two 75s in the U.S. Open.
"I've brought mum and dad to see where I had two great moments last year," said Allenby.

"First, where my pitch to four feet on the 18th got me into the playoff and then where I sank the 45-foot putt at the first extra hole to beat a great player like Bernhard Langer. That was one of the outstanding moments of my career.

"It would be nice to have more moments with my parents here and I'm looking for some form to be at a peak for the British Open. Then hopefully I can keep playing well to the end of the season in Europe and get back to how I was before the accident."
Montgomerie returns to Tour duty after a week's rest following his disappointment at finishing second behind Ernie Els in the U.S. Open.
The Scot will eye the 100,000 pounds ($167,000) first prize as he bids to finish as European number one for a record fifth successive time.
He trails European rankings leader Woosnam, who is not playing this week, by almost 180,000 pounds.
